messages:
elena (support): Hey team, escalando — paying customer (AcmeCorp / customer-jane) on dedicated EU fleet is seeing spikes of 429s during sustained bursts. They report it happens when traffic briefly routes to us-west failover. They included request IDs, a short repro, and a billing hit for repeated retries. Can eng-runtime take a look?

customer-jane: Repro steps we ran: 1) send 20 req/s for ~2m to eu-central endpoint, 2) after ~45s some requests get 429, 3) we see some requests routed to us-west with much higher latency then 429. Headers attached: X-Region-Hint: eu-central. We also saw a couple 401s earlier but that might be a separate token expiry.

elena (support): Repro snippets they gave:
```bash
# simple stress repro
for i in {1..120}; do \
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "X-Region-Hint: eu-central" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-open-3b","input":"hi"}' &\
  sleep 0.05
done
```
They also pasted part of the gateway log (trimmed):
```
[2026-11-02T14:12:05Z] req_id=abc123 src=eu-central routed=us-west status=429 reason=regional_capacity_exhausted
[2026-11-02T14:12:06Z] req_id=abc124 src=eu-central routed=eu-central status=200 latency_ms=110
[2026-11-02T14:12:06Z] req_id=abc125 src=eu-central routed=us-west status=504 latency_ms=1500
[2026-11-02T14:12:07Z] req_id=abc126 src=eu-central routed=us-west status=429 reason=quota_burst_exhausted
```

elena (support): Customer is on Dedicated EU pool (reservation_id: eu-ded-42) with burst credit enabled. They expected failover to EU-only or queueing, not cross-region fallback to US. They're worried about latency and billing for retries.

samir (eng-runtime): Thanks — pinging oncall @oncall-ryan and eng-platform. First glance: those log reasons (regional_capacity_exhausted / quota_burst_exhausted) indicate the EU dedicated pool hit its burst credits and the routing policy allowed cross-region fallback to region="any" which sent some traffic to us-west. That explains the high latency and 429s when the us-west pool couldn't accept the holding load.

samir (eng-runtime): Quick checks I ran from the control plane:
- EU dedicated pool utilization spiked to 100% around 14:11:40Z.
- Burst credit token bucket went to 0 at 14:12:02Z.
- Routing policy for this reservation is currently `fallback: [region, any]` (can fallback to other regions).

miguel (eng-platform): Confirming — the per-reservation per-region quota enforcement kicks in at the routing layer once local tokens are exhausted. Since fallback allows other regions, traffic is routed to nearest available compatible pool; if that target pool is also overloaded or has stricter quotas for cross-tenant routing we see 429s. We also recently changed the cross-region egress throttle config for some us-west nodes to protect spot capacity (rolled 2 weeks ago). That might have lowered effective capacity for cross-region failovers.

oncall-ryan: Notes from the on-call triage: customer impact is mid-high (application retries causing user-visible errors). Temporary mitigations: 1) disable cross-region fallback for this reservation (force local queueing), 2) top-up burst credits for eu-ded-42, or 3) add a temporary allocation to eu-ded pool. We can do (1) quickly in control plane; (2) requires billing approval but we can provision emergency credits for this customer for 1 hour.

elena (support): Customer asked for repro steps we can run on our side to validate. Suggested steps below; please sanity-check before I send: 1) use the curl loop above with X-Region-Hint header 2) set concurrency to 20-30 req/s for ~2 minutes 3) watch gateway logs for `reason=regional_capacity_exhausted` and `routed=us-west` 4) try with fallback disabled to confirm queueing instead of cross-region routes.

samir (eng-runtime): Sanity-check: good. Also add a small script to emit token-bucket status via our admin API to observe burst credits:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://control.redwood.ai/v1/reservations/eu-ded-42/burst_status
# returns {"tokens": 0, "last_refill": "2026-11-02T14:12:02Z"}
```
If tokens=0 and fallback=any -> expect cross-region routing to engage. If you set fallback to `region_only` the runtime will queue up to queue_size (configurable) instead of failing over.

miguel (eng-platform): For a longer-term fix we should: 1) make per-reservation fallback default to region_only for Dedicated by policy, 2) add clearer billing signals when emergency burst top-ups are used, and 3) adjust us-west cross-region throttle thresholds for protected nodes so they can accept emergency overflow from EU for short windows. I'll open a platform ticket.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20261102-73 assigned to eng-runtime and eng-platform.

customer-jane: Thanks — can you do option (1) now? We want to avoid cross-region routing while we run our load tests. Also if you can top-up for 30 minutes that would be great.

elena (support): @samir @miguel can we toggle fallback for eu-ded-42 to region_only now and do a one-time burst top-up? If yes I'll coordinate with the customer and run repro.

samir (eng-runtime): I'll flip fallback to region_only now (will take ~15s). After I change it, verify with this query:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://control.redwood.ai/v1/reservations/eu-ded-42/config
# look for "fallback":"region_only"
```
I can also authorize an emergency +5k burst token top-up for 30 minutes — just confirm with support.

samir (eng-runtime): Done — fallback set to region_only. Burst tokens incremented by 5000 with expiry +30m.

elena (support): Sending instructions to customer now. Will run their repro and paste results.

customer-jane (later): Ran the loop again. No cross-region routes observed. We still saw some 429s but they were queued and slowly drained (latency increased but no 504s). Thank you.

elena (support): Great. Follow-ups: - eng-platform to track platform ticket for permanent policy changes - eng-runtime to add a guard in control plane UI that warns when fallback=any for Dedicated reservations - support to document customer-facing guidance about burst credits vs. fallback behavior.

samir (eng-runtime): I'll add a small handler to surface fallback policy in the reservation page and add a warning banner. Logged ENG-PLT-856.

miguel (eng-platform): I'll own the longer-term throttle tuning and billing signal. Logged PLAT-4791.

elena (support): Closing loop with customer now. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
